questions.title: The Rooftop Garden
questions.text:
Every morning, Amara climbed the stairs to the roof of her apartment building. The roof was flat and gray, and the wind always smelled like bus exhaust. But Amara had a plan.

She started with one bucket of soil and three bean seeds from the library's seed swap. She watered them before school and again when she got home. For nine days, nothing happened. Her neighbor Mr. Ortiz told her that beans need warm soil, so she moved the bucket next to the warm air vent.

On the tenth day, a pale green hook pushed up through the dirt. Amara was so excited she almost dropped her backpack down the stairwell.

By June, the bean vines had climbed a string all the way up the railing. Mr. Ortiz brought two tomato plants. A girl from the fourth floor brought marigolds. The gray roof was turning green, one bucket at a time.
questions.source: An original story written for this worksheet.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the story?

options.why: The story never compares them. Think about what changes on the roof.

options.text: Amara does not like her apartment.
options.why: She works to make the roof better, not to leave it.

options.text: Amara's patience starts a garden that brings neighbors together.
options.why: Yes: her waiting paid off, and others joined in.

options.text: Mr. Ortiz is the best gardener in the building.
options.why: He helps, but the story is about what Amara starts.
